claim: intake.accept drops every line that still carries its trailing newline, so lines split with keepends are never accepted.
why: The pattern ends with $, which in Python also matches just before a final newline. So 'AB123\n' is a valid code and is accepted, and the claim is false. Reading the pattern, it looks like a strict full-string match, so the case is meant to reward running main.py and seeing AB123 with its newline kept in the output rather than recalling the rule.

root.claim: intake.accept drops every line that still carries its trailing newline, so lines split with keepends are never accepted.

atoms.claim: A code followed by a newline fails is_valid
atoms.evidence: Running main.py prints ['AB123\n', 'EF678']: the line 'AB123\n' was accepted because $ matches before a final newline.
It is absent from the output, but only because it has two digits, not because of the newline.
